text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt's credit worthiness and investment rating rise in a report by Standard and Poor's, which says that President Hosni Mubarak could mass political consensus behind the country's economic reforms. The report puts Egypt in the same category of industrial countries in East Europe and the Asian Tigers.
- Sudanese Vice President, al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh, arrived in Cairo on Wednesday.
- Egypt offers medical supplies to Afghanistan and takes part in an international forum to be held next Saturday to supply the country with urgent humanitarian aid worth $133 million.

- Mubarak spoke by telephone with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after the initialling of the Hebron deal. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says signing the agreement is a positive step.
- Eyewitnesses tell public prosecutor that negligence and high speed were the cause of the accident of the bus which veered off a Cairo bridge and sank into the mud on a Nile bank.
- The world hails Mubarak's role in the Hebron deal.
- A vehicle carrying the body of one of the bus victims to his burial had an accident and sank into a canal. Residents retrieved the body and brought it to the burial site.
